own_original_text:
Executive Order 11436
SUSPENDING THE PROVISIONS OF SECTION 6372 OF TITLE 10 OF THE  
UNITED STATES CODE, WHICH RELATE TO THE RETIREMENT OR RE­
TENTION ON THE ACTIVE LIST OF CERTAIN REAR ADMIRALS IN THE  
NAVY
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6386 (c) of title 10 
of the United States Code, I hereby suspend the provisions of section 
6372 of title 10 of the United States Code.
T h e W h it e H ouse ,
December 2, 1968.
[F.R. Doc. 68-14576 ; Filed, Dec. 3,1968 ; 10: 06 a.m.]

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11436 (signed 1968-12-02; 33 FR 17943, Federal Register of December 4, 1968) suspends section 6372 of title 10, United States Code (retirement or retention on the active list of certain rear admirals in the Navy), citing as its sole authority "section 6386 (c) of title 10" of the United States Code. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11436.txt, PDF page 7); its number, title and the December 4, 1968 issue line match the census register row, but the extracted text prints no page number, so I did not confirm the page 17943 citation from it. Its single operative sentence is the whole order, and it states no duration. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number; that express revocation is the first end. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; neither is the end because neither names EO 11436): (1) the National Emergencies Act, Pub. L. 94-412 (Sept. 14, 1976), whose section 101(a) terminated, two years after enactment, powers possessed as a result of national emergencies then in effect; its section 502(a)(8) provides that the Act shall not apply to "Sections 3313, 6386(c), and 8313 of title 10, United States" Code, so that termination did not reach the section 6386(c) authority this order rests on (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10976_Pub._L._94-412_National_Emergencies_Act_sec._101_a_90_Stat._1255_Sept._14_1976_status_d1e4940870.txt, text sha256 9af91c5062c556d26e97baaad68d89a4aa6cbfbb51937898bc13ef801d78a350). (2) The Defense Officer Personnel Management Act, Pub. L. 96-513 (Dec. 12, 1980), whose section 335 provides that "The following sections of chapter 573 are repealed:" and lists, among others, sections 6372 (the section this order suspends) and 6386 (the section whose subsection (c) is the order's authority), effective September 15, 1981 under section 701(a) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11436_Defense_Officer_Personnel_Management_Act_Pub._L._96-513_Dec._12_1980_94_Stat._2835_in_bdcccb89ac.txt, text sha256 c3ab6a35c6abc89d1a7cf8da82a3857809878054424edc8731240edb46dc7970). Section 702 of that Act preserves the suspended status of a provision that is amended, not repealed, so it does not apply to the repealed section 6372; section 703 preserves matured rights, penalties and proceedings. After September 15, 1981 the suspension had no statutory provision left to operate on, but under the ruling the repeal is a disclosed candidate, and the order's end remains the instrument that names it. The pre-1981 text of 10 U.S.C. 6372 and 6386(c) is not held, so no statutory duration limit on the suspension is shown either way. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; a search of held texts for section 6386(c) (which found the National Emergencies Act exclusion); the held text of Pub. L. 96-513 sections 335 and 701-703; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording: a scan of its full held text for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects. Personnel actions taken while the suspension was in force are completed acts that the held sources do not tie to the order's continuation; the suspension itself does not survive the revocation.

first_end.mechanism: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) orders that the listed Executive Orders, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:", in a two-column table headed 'No. Subject'; its entry "11436 Suspending provisions of section 6372 of title 10, U.S.C., relating to retirement or retention on the" names this order by number. A scan of the full held text of EO 12553 for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending finds those strings only inside table subjects (the words effectiveness and Suspending), not as operative wording, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, 1986-02-25; that is an inference from the heading and signature block, not express wording.
